  Mayor Pro Tem Alarcón spoke regarding support of residents and access to
  public facilities, special events, and parks. She provided three (3) suggestions:
  1) Create equity in the deposit structure so that the security deposit is the same
  for all parks; 2) Do not increase the fees for youth sports; and 3) Do not
  implement the special event fees for the Jolly Holiday activity wristband,
  Springfest activity wristband, and the Bingo Card fee.

  Recreation Manager Altobelli and Management Analyst I Kelley provided
  information to Council regarding the park fees and youth scholarships.
  Discussion ensued regarding disseminating scholarship information to schools
  and organizations, increased costs, use of American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA)
  funds, waiver or reduction of the general admission fee for the fireworks show,
  and the use of Measure AV funds for community events.

  Motion: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-043 as proposed with the exception of the
  park security deposit fees ensuring that they are applied equitably to all parks
  throughout the City; eliminate the increase in youth sports; eliminate wristband fee for
  Springfest and Jolly Holiday, and the Bingo Card fee; and consideration of an
  admission fee reduction for the 4th of July event in 2024.
  Moved by Andrea Alarcón, seconded by Austin Bishop.

ISSUE
City Council Nomination and Appointment of one (1) Alternate Member to the Human
Rights Advisory Committee.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code 2.08.030, the City Council
nominate and appoint one (1) individual to serve as the Alternate Member on the
Human Rights Advisory Committee for a term to expire on April 30, 2025.

  1. Mancilla, Tanya Janine Rincon (D5)  2. Sartika, Hestia (D4)
  3. Sigala, Belen (Out of District
  Boundaries)

BACKGROUND

The Human Rights Advisory Committee was created by the City Council to act in an
advisory capacity providing advice and actionable recommendations to the Mayor, City
Council and City Manager in their efforts to build a more inclusive community. Residency
in the City of Palmdale is not required.

DISCUSSION
The City Clerk’s Office was informed of the resignation of Covel Jenkins on June 15,
2023. The alternate, Elizabeth Henriquez, selected by Council at the April 5, 2023,
meeting has filled the position.

The alternate position must now be filled. There are three (3) remaining qualified
applicants who are interested in serving on the Committee. The applicant’s district is
listed for informational purposes only.

BACKGROUND
The purpose of the Housing Authority (HA) of the City of Palmdale is to address the
shortage of safe, sanitary housing for persons of low income. The term of office is two
(2) years. Housing Authority members are not involved in the management of the
Housing Authority properties. Members are subject to the provisions of the Ralph M.
Brown Act and are required to attend city-sponsored trainings.

The HA is comprised of seven (7) Commissioners, five (5) City Council members and
two (2) appointed Tenant members. Per California Health and Safety Code §34130(b),
at least one of the appointed tenant members must be age 62 or older. The tenant
members have the same equal voting rights as the five City Council members.

DISCUSSION
City Council directed staff to open a recruitment for the Housing Authority Tenant Member
Commissioners. A recruitment advertisement was placed in the AV Press for interested
citizens to apply. The Communications Division also provided a press release to the
public, including the application submittal deadline, and posted the advertisement on the
City’s Social Media pages. The Classified Ad and the application were made available on
the Board & Commission webpage and the Housing Authority webpage, as well as in the
Office of the City Clerk. Staff received thirteen applications, seven of the applications met
the qualifications.

This item is brought forth for City Council Nomination and Appointment of two Housing
Authority Tenant Member Commissioners for terms to expire September 2025.

A Livescan fingerprint submission via the California Department of Justice is required
for the appointment to be complete. The State of California requires a Statement of
Economic Interest Form 700 be filed within 30-days of the appointment.
